page0.text:
I wouldn't want anyone to get sad, if I can help it.
If I just use my own limited powers to make the people around me happy, the world will be a better place.
page0.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page0:1

page1.text:
That was always Kiritsugu's favorite saying.
The man who I saw as a champion of justice was saying he thought he was a failure, that he wasn't good enough.
page1.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page1:1

page2.text:
He didn't need to explain it to me.
The worlds the young me and the grown-up Kiritsugu lived in were too different, and so the standards for being a hero of justice were different too.
When I was young, this house was my entire world.
So my old man, Fuji-nee, myself, and my favorite shed were the only things that needed protecting.
page2.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page2:1

page3.text:
All I thought I had to protect was what I could see around me.
But Kiritsugu wanted to do something for those he couldn't see or reach.
page3.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page3:1

page4.text:
I was reckless when I was young.
I built myself up by cursing the cruel world.
The world was cruel...so I became cruel as a way to make my ideals a reality.
page4.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page4:1

page5.text:
There will always be those that can't be saved.
You just can't save everything.
If in the process of trying to save a thousand, you overlook five hundred...
...then I will abandon one hundred to save nine hundred.
That is the most efficient way.
"That is the ideal," Kiritsugu once told me.
page5.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page5:1

page6.text:
Of course I got mad hearing that.
It really ticked me off.
Because I didn't have to be told that since I knew that already.
Because I knew firsthand that it was that very ideal that led to me being saved.
page6.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page6:1

page7.text:
I didn't need to be reminded about something so obvious.
But I still believed that a hero of justice could save everyone, despite those limitations.
Because that's what a hero of justice was: someone who could still perform miracles, no matter how idealistic or unattainable they may be.
page7.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page7:1

page8.text:
You're right, Shirou.
Results are the most important thing. But apart from that, what's even more important is to have the heart—
page8.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page8:1

page9.text:
What did Kiritsugu say about heart, again?
...I don't remember.
It's not often I reminisce about something from so long ago.
I must be in a deep sleep.
Otherwise, I wouldn't be dreaming in the first place.
page9.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page9:1

page10.text: Shirou. Wake up. It's almost time for breakfast.
page10.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page10:1

page11.text:
See?
Saber is waking me up. It's pathetic.
page11.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page11:1

page12.text:
"...What!?"
I bolt upright and out of my futon.
It's six-thirty in the morning. Fresh sunlight pours in from outside.
"Shirou. It is morning. Do you need to prepare breakfast?"
Saber is staring right at me.
page12.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page12:1

page13.text:
"I overslept. Sorry. I'll get up right away."
"You have nothing to apologize for, but you have no time to relax. It appears Sakura and Rin were arguing earlier."
"Sakura and Tohsaka are arguing?"
page13.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page13:1

page14.text:
What's going on?
Hold on. Don't throw me into a situation I don't understand just as I'm waking up.
page14.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page14:1

page15.text:
"Is that happening in Tohsaka's room?"
"No, the living room. I just passed by, so I do not know the details."
"Got it. I'll head there now."
page15.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page15:1

page16.text:
Oh but...
There's something I forgot to do.
"What is it, Shirou?"
"Good morning, Saber. Thanks for waking me."
I greet her, and then I head out to the hallway.
...But seriously, what the hell did Tohsaka do to start an argument with Sakura!?
page16.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page16:1

page17.text:
"Tohsaka!"
In the living room...
There's no sign of Sakura. Tohsaka is alone, casually watching the weather forecast on TV.
page17.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page17:1

page18.text:
"Morning. What a way to start the morning, shouting my name like that."
She turns around, as if to ask if something had happened.
page18.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page18:1

page19.text:
Huh?
That's weird. It doesn't look like she was fighting with Sakura at all.
page19.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page19:1

page20.text: "Uh...morning. Hey, Tohsaka. I heard you and Sakura were arguing. Is that true?"
page20.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page20:1

page21.text:
"Huh? Oh, from Saber.
Yes, it may have seemed that way, to an outside observer, but it was nothing, really. I just told her not to come here for a while."
page21.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page21:1

page22.text:
"Gh—!?"
Sh-she's so casual about basically banning Sakura from my house!
page22.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page22:1

page23.text: "That's ridiculous. Sakura already said no to staying away from this house, so there's no way she would agree even if we asked again—"
page23.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page23:1

page24.text: "She wouldn't agree, but she went home after I presented her with a compromise. I told her I would go back home without argument if she stays away for a week. She agreed to those terms. She went home, even if she was a little reluctant. Oh right, she sends her regards."
page24.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page24:1

page25.text:
"You did what...?"
Why would she do something like that without telling me...?
...
Actually, I shouldn't yell at her for it.
Tohsaka's just done something I should have.
page25.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page25:1

page26.text:
"You're right. Sorry for making you be the bad guy so early in the morning. You must feel terrible, Tohsaka."
"Huh? No, it wasn't bad or unpleasant to me. Why would you think that, Shirou?"
page26.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page26:1

page27.text:
"Uh, because weren't you and Sakura friends? Telling Sakura to leave not once, but twice, doesn't sound like a fun job.
That's why I feel bad. I'm the one who should take charge, but I made you do the dirty work again."
page27.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page27:1

page28.text:
"Th-that's fine. I just kicked out Sakura for my own safety. There's no reason for you to apologize."
"Huh? What do you mean, for your own safety?"
page28.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page28:1

page29.text:
"Well, you said Shinji's a Master, right?
Knowing him, if Shinji finds out Sakura comes here, he'll target this place, so it's best to keep Sakura away from here until we've finished dealing with Shinji."
page29.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page29:1

page30.text:
"Ah..."
I get it.
She makes a good point.
Shinji said he doesn't tell Sakura anything. I don't think he was lying.
But if he finds out his little sister comes here so often, he might get the wrong idea.
page30.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page30:1

page31.text: "You're right. It could look to Shinji like we're taking Sakura hostage."
page31.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page31:1

page32.text:
"Exactly. But more importantly, this place is still dangerous.
I wouldn't want her to be walking around at night, so it's best for her to stay away from here for a while. This is for Sakura's own safety, as well as ours."
page32.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page32:1

page33.text:
"...Yeah, you're right. I feel bad for Sakura, but I'll just have to apologize and ask her forgiveness later."
Though I won't be able to explain myself even when the time comes.
page33.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page33:1

page34.text:
"...Hnnn."
This is really getting to me.
I feel really bad about turning Sakura away like this, even if it's temporary. She's been so unselfish about helping me for all this time.
page34.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page34:1

page35.text: "Oh, you look really down. What happened to all that energy you had when you shouted at me earlier? Are you all sad and lonely, not having Sakura around?"
page35.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page35:1

page36.text:
Tohsaka grins maliciously.
Oh crap. I've known she'd tease me whenever I show vulnerability, but I went and did it again.
page36.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page36:1

page37.text: "Hmph. Leave me alone. Sakura was the symbol of peace at our house. She offset whatever Fuji-nee and I were lacking. So of course I'm down about us sending her away for our own selfish reasons."
page37.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page37:1

page38.text:
"Oh, so you do understand. If you can say that much, then you pass. I'd say you're starting to get more determined."
"Huh? Wh-what are you trying to say?"
page38.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page38:1

page39.text:
"Don't you get it? Once this war ends, Sakura will come back.
You say you don't want the Holy Grail, but that just means you should fight to take back the peaceful life you had before. See? Now you have a clear goal."
Tohsaka smiles her very biggest smile.
page39.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page39:1

page40.text:
...
When she puts it like that, I really have no choice but to agree.
Damn. I don't know what to say.
What she said there confirms that she's both mean-spirited and ridiculously awesome at the same time.
page40.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page40:1

page41.text:
"What? So Sakura won't be coming here for a while?"
"Yeah, that's what's going on. Why don't you do your parents a favor and go home once in a while for a change? Gramps was complaining about his daughter neglecting him."
page41.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page41:1

page42.text:
"Leave Dad out of this. He's not going to die or anything, whether I'm there or not.
And with Sakura gone, I have to be even more vigilant! You're still a boy, so if anything fishy happens here, I'll be the one who gets in trouble and even loses her job. If that happens, are you going to take responsibility, Shirou?"
page42.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page42:1

page43.text:
"That'll never happen—"
...Sadly, since I'm a man, I can't really confidently deny that...
page43.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page43:1

page44.text:
"Emiya? Why'd you just stop?"
She glares.
Tohsaka's eyes bore into me from one side.
"...I don't think anything would happen. Tohsaka's not staying here for fun, you know.
I sure know that."
page44.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page44:1

page45.text:
"Good. I'm glad to hear that. Sounds like Emiya is trustworthy, Miss Fujimura."
"Of course. Even from my point of view, Shirou is really composed. So much so, he might be overdoing it."
page45.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page45:1

page46.text:
"..."
Saber continues to eat in silence as she observes the two interacting.
It's been two days, but I don't think I'll ever get used to this.
page46.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page46:1

page47.text:
"Oh I forgot to tell you, Shirou. It's about the kyudou club. Did you hear Mitsuzuri got hurt?"
"Mitsuzuri? Did she pick a fight with someone in another club again? Honestly, she really needs to calm down. She's going to be a third year soon.
So how's she doing? Is she hurt bad?"
page47.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page47:1

page48.text:
"No, she's fine. She just sprained her ankle. She was apparently attacked by some shady guy on her way home.
You know she runs fast. She made a mad dash, but it sounds like she fell and got hurt."
page48.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page48:1

page49.text:
"I see. I'm glad nothing bad happened. But honestly, whoever tried to attack her is either a real daredevil, or they're just reckless.
Either way, they were a fool. I just thought..."
"You thought she would have knocked the culprit out rather than run?"
Fuji-nee grins.
Yep. She sure knows Ayako Mitsuzuri well.
page49.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page49:1

page50.text:
"Yeah. It's rare for Mitsuzuri to run away.
But I guess she's not so tough against thieves. I suppose things worked out for the best. Something like that will probably teach her a thing or two about being feminine."
I munch on my rice, nodding approvingly.
page50.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page50:1

page51.text:
"Hey Emiya."
Suddenly...
Rin Tohsaka slaps my shoulder, smiling at me.
page51.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page51:1

page52.text:
"I have some news for you."
"Huh? What? I doubt it'll be more interesting than what I just heard."
page52.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page52:1

page53.text:
"Yeah. I never mentioned this before, but Ayako and I are real good friends. Did you know we're close enough that we hang out on the weekends?"
Wait.
Why are she and Mitsuzuri friends?
page53.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page53:1

page54.text:
"Come again?"
"Oh, don't worry. I'm going to make sure I tell her every single word you just said. I'm sure if I tell her about how happy Emiya was when he heard about her predicament, why, I bet she'll break ten stacks of tiles from sheer delight!"
page54.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page54:1

page55.text: "...I...would like to amend my statement. See, it was just a figure of speech. It's not something I'd be proud if people heard, so I would really appreciate if you kept it to yourself."
page55.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page55:1

page56.text:
"Oh really? Well, I could keep quiet about it, but it would be reeeally hard for me to do that unless there was, maybe, something in it for me. I might just accidentally slip up, you know?"
"I can't believe this. Sure, you sound sincere, but I'm not buying it."
page56.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page56:1

page57.text:
"Oh I'm sorry. Don't get me wrong. I'm not playing around here."
Yeah, there's no misunderstanding here.
She's enjoying this.
page57.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page57:1

page58.text:
"Got it. I'll start making Western-style breakfasts from now on.
You said it earlier. You mentioned that breakfast should have bread."
page58.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page58:1

page59.text:
"Good. And I think some jams, apart from marmalade, would be nice...like strawberry jam."
"...I don't know what you have against Japanese breakfasts, you foreigner wannabe. I can't believe you would so radically change our breakfast just to suit your needs, you tyrant."
page59.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page59:1

page60.text:
"That is not entirely true. I would also be pleased to have bread served at breakfast. Soft-boiled eggs would also be an excellent addition."
Saber jumps right into the discussion.
page60.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page60:1

page61.text:
"Is that so? Fine. You all just want Western-style food, dammit. Sakura makes a Western-style breakfast one time and it goes right to your heads.
Fine then, I'll serve bread for tomorrow, so no more complaints, right? So what was said here, stays here. Don't you dare blab about this to Mitsuzuri."
page61.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page61:1

page62.text:
I huff, and shove rice into my mouth without looking at either of them.
And then...
"Why would you be doing something so pointless?"
Fuji-nee, who had been watching our conversation with a look of wonderment, finally speaks up.
page62.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page62:1

page63.text:
"What, what do you mean, pointless?"
"Even if Tohsaka isn't going to say anything, I'm going to tell Mitsuzuri anyway. No way would I pass up talking about something so interesting."
Fuji-nee shakes her head disapprovingly as she eats.
"..."
Actually.
I need to think of a way to deal with her, or I'm really in trouble.
page63.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page63:1

page64.text:
Breakfast ends, and it's seven-thirty.
Fuji-nee surprisingly stays back and suggests that the three of us walk to school.
page64.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page64:1

page65.text:
...
...But we can't do that.
I made a decision last night.
Now that I've said I won't rely on Saber, I can't afford to take it easy anymore.
page65.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page65:1

page66.text:
"Then let's go. Did you lock up, Shirou?"
"No, don't worry about locking up. I'm not going to school today."
I wave Fuji-nee and Tohsaka off.
page66.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page66:1

page67.text:
Fuji-nee freezes, stupefied for just a few seconds.
"What!? What do you mean you're not going to school!?"
"Eh, huh?"
Tohsaka beat Fuji-nee to the chase.
page67.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page67:1

page68.text:
"Th-that's right. You don't look sick enough to miss school today, Shirou."
"No, but my scar hurts. You know how scars hurt when the weather changes? It's like that."
page68.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page68:1

page69.text:
"Hm... You're lying, Shirou."
"Yeah, but let me off the hook just for today, Fuji-nee. It's not that I don't like school. There's something I have to do, and it's just more important right now. So let me go."
page69.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page69:1

page70.text:
"...Oh come on, how can I respond if you are going to put it like that? You always were cagey when you had something really important to take care of."
Fuji-nee is complaining, but at least she understands.
page70.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page70:1

page71.text:
"So there it is. I'll leave the school to you, Tohsaka."
"O-okay. Not much is going to change just because you're not there. That's not a bad idea, Emiya."
page71.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page71:1

page72.text:
"Yeah, leave the house to me. I'm not going to work for a while either, so I won't be leaving the house much."
"Got it. Then I'm heading out, Shirou. If you're going to skip school because you're hurt, you shouldn't leave the house much."
"Well, see you. I'm giving you a pass today, but you're going to have to discuss this with me beforehand next time."
page72.sourceUnit: セイバールート七日目-00:page72:1
